subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 7: Switch On – You and your phone (video interviews and project)
outcomes: Understand people's ideas about a week without a phone.
Hear and say the difference between I, I'd and I'll.
Compare life in the 1980s with life now and present my group's ideas.

tf.s: Maxwell mentions writing to people offline.
tf.why: He talks about writing to people without the internet.

tf.s: Sophie says she would be early every day without her phone.
tf.why: Sophie says she would be late every day.

tf.s: Jack seemed relaxed about a week without his phone.
tf.why: He isn't on it much and likes camps with the scouts.

tf.s: 'I'll' is the short form of 'I will'.
'I'd' is the short form of 'I will'.
tf.why: I'd is the short form of 'I would' (or I had).

tf.s: To find the average phone time, you add the times and divide by the number of people.
tf.why: That's how we calculate an average.

tf.s: Teenagers in the 1980s used mobile phones to chat to friends.
tf.why: They didn't have mobile phones; they used landline phones.

tf.s: 'Keep in touch' means stay in contact with someone.
tf.why: We keep in touch by calling, writing or meeting.

tf.s: A disadvantage of a week without a phone is that it can be harder to contact online friends.
The small difference between I, I'd and I'll is impossible to hear.
tf.why: It is small, but you can hear it with practice.

boxes.q: Which speaker mentions writing to people offline?
Which speaker says she would be late every day without her phone?
boxes.why: Sophie uses her phone to be on time.

boxes.q: Complete: I think ___ be quite bored. (prediction)
boxes.why: I'll = I will, for a prediction.

boxes.q: Complete: ___ probably hang out with them.
boxes.why: I'd = I would, for an imagined situation.

boxes.q: How did teenagers chat to friends in the 1980s?
boxes.why: Mobile phones and the internet weren't common then.

boxes.q: Complete: In the 1980s, people ___ (buy) tickets at the stadium.

o: plan when and where to meet
boxes.why: We make arrangements to meet people.

boxes.q: Which is an advantage of a week without a phone?
o: more time for homework and sleep
boxes.why: Less phone time can mean more time for other things.

boxes.q: Which sentence compares then and now?
o: Buying tickets is easier now than in the 1980s.

mcq.q: What did groups calculate in Ex 1?
o: the number of apps in the world
mcq.why: They worked out the group's average phone time.

mcq.q: What does the video ask the speakers about?
mcq.why: The interviews are about a week without a phone.

mcq.q: How did people get holiday information in the 1980s?
o: from newspapers, phone calls and visiting places
mcq.why: There were no smartphones, so people used other ways.

mcq.q: Which speaker seemed relaxed about a week without a phone?
mcq.why: Jack isn't on his phone much.

mcq.q: Complete: If I didn't have my phone, ___ write letters to my friends.
mcq.why: An imagined situation uses would: I'd.

mcq.q: Complete: Don't worry, ___ call you later.
mcq.why: A promise or decision uses will: I'll.

mcq.q: Three friends use their phones for 2, 3 and 4 hours a day. What is the average?
Why did Jack think a week without his phone would be nice?
o: He isn't on it much and enjoys camps with the scouts
He wants to sleep all day

mcq.q: Which is a way life was better without phones?
o: People met face to face more and had less screen time
mcq.why: Less screen time meant more real-life contact.

mcq.q: Which is a way life is better now with phones?
o: We can contact people quickly and buy tickets online
